__inputs.label: Prometheus
__inputs.description: Grafana Cloud metrics, where the OTLP metric exporter writes.

__inputs.name: DS_TEMPO
__inputs.label: Tempo
__inputs.description: Grafana Cloud traces. Latency and error rate come from spans rather than from a metric, because the SPEC metric table has no duration histogram and inventing one would put the same number in two places.

panels.title: Cost equivalent, selected range
panels.description: Counterfactual, at published list prices. Real spend on these free tiers is zero, so this is a comparison quantity and not money.

panels.title: Sessions
panels.description: Sessions that made at least one priced model call. A session that never called a model records no cost observation, so this undercounts total runs on purpose rather than reporting them as free.

panels.title: Export failures
panels.description: The only signal that tracing itself has stopped. Anything above zero means spans are not arriving, and every other panel here is then reporting less than happened.

panels.title: Detections by type
panels.description: Zero here means one of two things and this panel cannot tell you which: nothing fired, or nothing could fire. Two of the three detectors need tool spans, and a workload that emits none reports zero forever. Check the denominator in study/coverage.md before reading this as health.

panels.title: Tokens by direction
panels.description: Input and output are priced separately, so they are counted separately. A single total cannot be turned back into a cost.

panels.title: Latency by operation, p50 and p95
panels.description: From spans, not from a metric. A session span encloses whatever the host does before its work starts, including waiting for a concurrency slot, so read the model and tool spans for provider latency and the session span for wall clock. study/traces.md, trace 2.

panels.title: Error rate by operation
panels.description: Spans that ended ERROR. `error.type` is the exception class, never the message, so this groups without unbounded cardinality.
